candidates.description: A calculated ratio of the absolute neutrophil count to the absolute lymphocyte count, used as a marker of systemic inflammation.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Search the Laboratory Results or CBC section for 'NLR' or 'Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio' and extract the reported numerical value.
candidates.measurement_definition: The numerical ratio of neutrophils to lymphocytes, reported as a unitless decimal value.
candidates.name: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the NLR was calculated using a standardized formula across different laboratory reports is not explicitly stated.

citations.quote: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with lepidic and acinar components

candidates.description: The histopathological classification of the lung malignancy based on cellular morphology and immunohistochemical markers.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Review the 'Final Diagnosis', 'Histology', or 'Microscopic Examination' sections of the pathology report to identify the tumor subtype.
candidates.measurement_definition: Classification as 'Adenocarcinoma' (typically TTF-1 positive, Napsin A positive) or 'Squamous cell carcinoma' (typically p40 positive, CK5/6 positive).
candidates.name: Histologic Subtype
candidates.uncertainty: The evidence mentions 'moderately differentiated' and 'poorly differentiated' as grades; it is uncertain if grading should be captured as a separate variable or bundled into the subtype.

limitations: Limited number of patients presented in the evidence fragments.
Lack of standardized reporting for NLR across all records (some provided as calculations, others as results).
summary: The provided evidence identifies measurable baseline variables in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), specifically focusing on the inflammatory marker Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR) and the histologic subtype of the tumor (Adenocarcinoma vs. Squamous Cell Carcinoma).
